title: Trying to get my sister more info films and tv

commenti.body: I would say There Will Be Blood is a great one to work towards but maybe not immediately. Other top of mind choices Before Sunrise, Chungking Express, La Haine, Misery, Bad Lieutenant.  Just a freestyle of great flicks

Hmm maybe Baby Driver. Gone Girl could be jumping-off point to eventual darker big films like Midsommar, No Country for Old Men. 

Unsure how old your sister is, but I also found To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before to be a cute and well done film with techniques that stand out (directing/cinematography/editing) enough to point them out to a newcomer.
She’s 15 so maybe not gone girl yet. (But maybe if she thinks it looks good than I have no problem seeing it with her). Baby driver is a pretty good choice.
Love all those films but I think most of them will be too much for her. But maybe the before trilogy
Yea I'd definitely encourage that one. Explodes a love for life + top notch film making

The Royal Tenenbaums        
Lars and the Real Girl   
The Truman Show    
Captain Fantastic    
Good Morning      
 
 Not sure what I would recommend for TV shows, but as far as movies go these seem like they would be pretty safe bets for someone who is just getting into movies and also enjoyed Little Miss Sunshine.  

Not a movie or a show, but the play No Exit by Jean-Paul Sartre might also be worth looking into. The Good Place draws from it very heavily.

Do you know what she’s really liked so far? And why she liked it? 

I feel like if you try to use her genuine interests to your advantage then that’d help make it clearer as to what direction to go in. 

I would get her thoughts on some of the things you’ve watched and then pick out some movies, and let her pick the ones she’s interested in. 

I suppose my recommendations would be:

Moonrise Kingdom
Amelie 
Arrival 
Dune 
Midnight in Paris
About Time
Pan’s Labyrinth 
Whiplash 
La La Land

Oh we watched whiplash or at least tried but she said it was too intense for her.

So from what we watched I think severance she liked the most only because I think it was very unique
I love all the films you recommended

I’ve never met someone who didn’t really enjoy The Martian. I feel like it’s a perfect mix of all star cast, intriguing concept and setting, thrills and laughs, and you just feel good after the credits roll.
